source.title: Deep Learning Through the Lens of Example Difficulty
source.authors: R. Baldock; Hartmut Maennel; Behnam Neyshabur

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests learning order under partial label corruption using training and hidden-layer k-NN learning curves, rather than testing the original random-label fitting setup.
record.gate_note: The paper trains VGG16 on CIFAR10 with 40% fixed randomized labels and describes training and inference learning curves. It does not test complete random labeling, an increasing noise-fraction sweep, or the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures learning order under 40% label corruption, testing V6. Its unregularized models' test accuracies also bear on the generalization-without-regularization part of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the label-corruption result: examples initially follow their original classes and subsequently acquire their assigned random labels, with an analogous progression across hidden-layer probes. This is a local experimental conclusion; the paper's broader conclusion concerns prediction depth and example difficulty.
record.recipe_differences: Uses partial fixed label randomization and hidden-layer k-NN probes to study learning order, rather than the original complete random-label fitting test.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported result is for CIFAR10, VGG16, 40% fixed randomized labels, and five random seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Original-class recognition precedes random-label recognition across layers of the converged network's k-NN probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under partial label corruption, earlier representations preserve class structure while later representations accommodate assigned noisy labels.

record.problems: The relevant label-noise result uses one corruption fraction; the paper does not report numerical values in the prose for the plotted curves or establish perfect fit of the randomized-label examples.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes identified beyond the training and inference learning curves in Figure 5.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian inputs.
Perfect training fit across corruption fractions and steadily increasing test error toward chance.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and the causal effect of removing individual regularizers relative to matched controls.
Learning order beyond VGG16 on CIFAR10 with 40% fixed randomized labels, including wholly random-label training.

missing.what: True-label VGG16 test accuracies without explicit regularization: SVHN 95%, Fashion MNIST 93%, CIFAR10 83%, and CIFAR100 45%. Record the dataset-specific outcomes separately; these establish performance without regularization, not the effect of removing it.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of a corruption sweep is untested coverage, not evidence limiting V4. Layerwise processing alone cannot establish temporal learning order. No numerical curve values were inferred from the extracted figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels across the training set and near-zero training error with test error at chance.
Training-time cost of fitting random versus true labels and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Only 40% fixed randomized labels are tested; no sweep from none to all corruption, no claim that training fit remains perfect, and no quantified test-error trend.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
The study uses one 40% fixed-random-label setting and describes learning order, but does not compare fully random labels with wholly real labels across training.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR10 with 40% fixed randomized labels; tracked training accuracy over epochs for unchanged-label data, randomized-label data, original labels of randomized examples, and test data.
rows.measure: Training accuracy learning curves; text says randomized examples are initially processed as their original class, then the network begins learning their assigned random labels, and a maximum is observed in training accuracy.
rows.value: Figure only for curve values; text describes initial original-class processing followed by learning the assigned random labels.
rows.note: The text describes the sequence but does not state numerical accuracy values or that training accuracy reaches 100%.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports original-class learning before assigned random-label learning; missing numerical accuracies do not make this ordering partial. Remove V4: this experiment does not establish perfect training fit or degradation across corruption fractions. The reported accuracy maximum should not be interpreted as a maximum followed by declining accuracy against assigned training labels.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Measured k-NN probe accuracy across layers on unchanged-label training data, randomized-label training data, original labels of randomized examples, and test data for the trained model.
rows.measure: Inference learning curve: sequence of k-NN probe accuracy values across layers; text says the training-curve phenomena also occur in this curve.
rows.value: Figure only; text states that the described phenomena also occur in the inference learning curve.
rows.note: The paper defines the inference learning curve as k-NN probe accuracies as data passes through the network; numerical curve values are not stated in prose.
rows.check: Layerwise k-NN accuracy measures processing within a trained network, rather than learning order over training. It independently establishes neither V6's temporal ordering nor V4's noise-fraction relationship. Appendix A.4 reports uncertainty across five runs.

relationships.condition: VGG16 on CIFAR10 with 40% fixed randomized labels, five seeds
relationships.reason: R1 and Section 3.2 report that corrupted examples initially receive their original classes before their assigned random labels are learned.
relationships.display_finding: Corrupted examples initially received their original classes before the network learned their assigned random labels.

relationships.condition: True-label VGG16 training without weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on SVHN, Fashion MNIST, and CIFAR10
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: Table 2 reports test accuracies of 95%, 93%, and 83%, respectively, demonstrating useful generalization without these regularizers.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracies reached 95% on SVHN, 93% on Fashion MNIST, and 83% on CIFAR10 without these regularizers.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
